text:
Maya L: Heads up — after the Ariadne-3 rollout at ~09:12 UTC we're seeing p99 latency for long-context requests (>=8k tokens) jump ~3x. Affects /v1/generate only. Customers complaining.
Ian K: Copy, any specific customer or batch that reproduces?
Maya L: Sending sample request/response IDs in a sec. Noticed it correlates with tokenizer update: bpe-normalize-2026-03-16.
Support Bot: 3 open tickets linked: RT-8742, RT-8745, RT-8751 (customer-visible errors: high latency).
Maya L: Paste of aggregated tail metrics:
```
window=09:10-09:40
model=ariadne-3
seq_len>=8000: p50=220ms p95=860ms p99=3120ms
previous (ariadne-2 longctx): p99=980ms
kvcache_miss_rate increased from 4% -> 27%
```
Devon R: kvcache miss spike + tokenizer change -> suspect token expansion (more subtokens => longer KV chains). Any tokenizer diffs?
Maya L: Tokenizer diff is small: normalization tweak for unicode NFKC + aggressive splitting on emoji clusters. Might be creating more tokens for our long messages.
SRE Ops: I pulled traces for a few samples, attaching span summary: majority of extra time spent in runtime::apply_kv_cache and decoder_step. There are repeated cache loads for extended sequences.
Ian K: Can you paste a sample token counts before/after for same input?
Maya L: Sure:
```
input_id=US-12345
ariadne-2: tokens=9100
ariadne-3 (new tokenizer): tokens=15640
```
Ian K: Oh wow that explains the extra token generation and cache pressure. More than 1.7x token increase.
Devon R: Mitigation options: 1) rollback tokenizer commit on canary 2) force route customer traffic to ari-3-small (shorter context variant) 3) enable model fallback to ari-2 for requests >8k tokens.
Maya L: Can we do a quick canary rollback? deploy-bot, who owns the rollout?
deploy-bot: Canary group 2 deployment flagged. Initiating rollback of bpe-normalize-2026-03-16 on ariadne-3 canary nodes. ETA ~3m. :gear:
SRE Ops: Starting temporary autoscale to absorb burst and bump kvcache size on canary hosts (+20%) to ease pressure while rollback completes.
Support Bot: Notifying customers: "we're rolling back a tokenizer change and routing you to a stable variant; ETA 15m" :email:
Maya L: After rollback (09:18): p99 dropped to ~1100ms for samples, p95 ~880ms. Still elevated vs previous baseline but far better.
Eva P: Good. Next steps: run tokenization A/B tests against representative corpora before shipping normalization changes. Also add a gate to disallow tokenizer that increases average token count by >20% for long-context models.
Devon R: Agreed. Also add automatic fallback config snippet so we can route requests over threshold to stable model. Example route patch:
```json
{"rules": [{"if": "input_tokens > 8000", "route_to": "ariadne-2", "reason": "tokenizer_longctx_fallback"}]}
```
Ian K: FYI tracing shows a small number of clients still hitting ariadne-3 longctx pods during rollback; we're draining them now.
Maya L: Customer-facing ticket updated with mitigation and RCA-in-progress.
SRE Ops: Locking this until we add a regression check in CI for token inflation and a kvcache-miss alert tied to tokenizer rollouts.
Support Bot: Tickets RT-8742/8745/8751 updated. Customers notified.
Eva P: Assigning owners: Maya (customer comms + token repro), Devon (route/fallback config), Ian (tracing + metrics dashboard), SRE Ops (infra sizing + kvcache thresholds). Postmortem due in 72h.
Maya L: Quick blurb for the postmortem: root cause appears to be NFKC normalization + emoji cluster splitting increasing token counts, causing KV cache eviction and decoder extra work for long-context requests -> p99 regression.
Devon R: We'll also add a canary heuristic: block tokenizer changes that increase 95th percentile token count for inputs >4k by >15% during canary window.
Ian K: For follow-up, I'll add a synthetic long-context workload to the canary harness.
Maya L: Thanks team. :thumbsup: Keeping thread open until postmortem posted.
